svg.aria-label: and the window's answer differs by 4
svg.text: The watermark, computed two ways — heuristic and perfect
heuristic reaches 185 and publishes 15 · perfect stalls at 50 and publishes 19
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed · key = which SOURCE it came from
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the straggler
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the assumed worst-case skew, in seconds. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: W0 — the window this chapter follows. W0 = 0 ([12:00, 12:02))
12 // primitive: KEYS — the source names. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
13 // primitive: max(xs) — the largest element. max([1, 3, 2]) = 3
14 // primitive: min(xs) — the smallest element. min([1, 3, 2]) = 1
15 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the WIN-second window holding et.
17 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those event ids.
19 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
23 // function: heuristic(events) — max event time seen so far, minus LAG, after
24 // each arrival. Monotonic because max() cannot shrink.
37 // function: perfect(events) — the largest time for which no EARLIER event is
38 // still to come. It reads events[i+1 ..], which a live pipeline cannot do.
45 if (smallest == NONE || events[j].et < smallest) { smallest = events[j].et }
52 // function: closeW0(wm) — the first index at which a watermark lets W0 fire,
53 // and what W0 holds at that moment.
60 if (wm[i] >= W0 + WIN) { return Trace(wm, i, sum(ids)) }
65 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the same window, under both watermarks.
Step 4/0 — and the window's answer differs by 4
`closeW0` is given a watermark array and nothing else — it does not know which generator produced it. With the heuristic it returns at `i` = 4 with 15; with the
perfect one at `i` = 7 with 19. `priceSeconds` = 34: that is what the correct answer costs, and it required reading the future.
